query: How can we reduce declined expense submissions?

per_column.name: asset_category_type
per_column.rationale: Categorizing submissions by asset type (hardware/travel/software) gives a real grouping axis to see if declines cluster by category. Values are soundly derived from short_description and ci in all samples.

per_column.name: submission_origin
per_column.rationale: Distinguishing manual vs auto-generated submissions is a useful axis for decline analysis. However groundedness is weaker: 'Deployed service-related asset' labeled 'auto_generated' and 'Miscellaneous hardware component' labeled 'manual_acquisition' rest on inference the terse text only loosely supports.

per_column.name: submission_action_type
per_column.rationale: A finer-grained action taxonomy could help, but it partly overlaps submission_origin. Some assignments seem inferred beyond the text (e.g. 'Miscellaneous hardware component' -> 'registration', a Dell laptop 'Asset assignment' -> 'allocation' is reasonable but others are shaky).

per_column.name: source_id_present
per_column.rationale: A bare presence flag on an existing original column (source_id). Mostly a trivial derivation with limited analytical leverage for reducing declines, though a null-source pattern could weakly correlate. Values are directly checkable and grounded.

per_column.name: ci_specificity
per_column.rationale: Classifying how specific the CI reference is (specific_model vs generic_label) is a plausible driver of declines (vague submissions may be rejected). Values track the ci text well across samples.

per_column.name: asset_brand_family
per_column.rationale: Vendor/brand extraction gives a genuine grouping axis. Brands are read soundly from ci/short_description; 'other_vendor' for silent rows is acceptable behaviour.

per_column.name: submitting_department
per_column.rationale: This largely duplicates the original 'department' column, and the produced values (e.g. 'Sales' for a plain hardware component, 'Product Management' for a Dell laptop) are not supported by any source text field shown — they appear invented rather than extracted.

per_column.name: is_high_cost_asset_type
per_column.rationale: A cost-tier flag could correlate with declines and adds a modeling axis. Assignments are a reasonable heuristic from asset type (laptop/desktop=True, RAM component/service=False), though it partly restates asset_category_type.

judge.rationale: Most added columns provide genuine new grouping/modeling axes relevant to diagnosing declined submissions (asset category, brand, CI specificity, origin, cost tier). Weaknesses: submitting_department largely duplicates an existing column and its values appear fabricated rather than extracted; source_id_present is a trivial presence flag; and origin/action_type contain some inferences the terse source text only loosely supports. Overall the set is useful and mostly grounded, with a couple of columns dragging groundedness down.
